abstracts.value: Fluctuations of conserved charges are a primary tool in the search for the QCD critical endpoint, but their beam-energy dependence is complicated by global baryon-number conservation, whose influence changes as the experimental acceptance covers different fractions of the collision system. We propose using correlations of net-baryon fluctuations between two separated rapidity windows to exploit the distinct signatures of conservation and critical dynamics. Global conservation produces a negative cross-window correlation, whereas a common long-wavelength critical fluctuation produces a positive one. We show that, within a canonical independent-source framework, the conservation-induced background and the critical signal enter additively at leading order, allowing the leading conservation term to be estimated and subtracted. The resulting yield-scaled correlator follows the nonmonotonic enhancement of an Ising-mapped equilibrium correlation length along a freeze-out trajectory passing near a hypothetical critical endpoint, while wider rapidity windows reduce the response through thermal smearing. Cross-rapidity cumulants therefore provide a rapidity-differential strategy for reducing the leading conservation background and sharpening fluctuation-based searches for QCD criticality in beam-energy-scan experiments.

titles.title: Unveiling QCD Criticality with Cross-Rapidity Net-Baryon Cumulants

abstracts.value: Theoretical models suggest that the adiabatic growth of a black hole immersed in dark matter can lead to the formation of high density regions of dark matter, known as ``spikes'', near the black hole event horizon. The density of these spikes is determined theoretically and observationally to be a power law of the form $ρ(r) \propto r^{-γ_\text{sp}}$. It has been shown that the spike can potentially have a detectable impact on the emitted gravitational waves and shadow radius of the central black hole. In this work, we model the dark matter spike using a real scalar field with a non-standard potential. More specifically we ``reverse engineer'' the equations of motion to find a potential for the scalar field that permits a solution to the equations of motion with desired energy density and reasonable background geometry. We show that the emerging geometry is testable. In addition, the fact that the solution is derived from a covariant action makes it possible to study gravitational perturbations of the black hole in the presence of a spike including the backreaction of the spike.

titles.title: Scalar Field Model for Dark Matter Spikes Surrounding Sgr A$^*$ and M87$^*$

abstracts.value: Fault-tolerant quantum computation fundamentally relies on encoding a logical qubit into a structured block of physical qubits, typically in the tens to hundreds. As a trade-off for improved fault-tolerance, logical gate operations will incur a linear overhead in terms of both the amount of time and quantum resources than before. For example, in monolithic quantum computing, performing a gate operation on two distant logical qubits will first require using a linear number of SWAP operations in order to move the logical qubits next to each other; while in distributed quantum computing, doing so will first require a linear number of ancilla qubits in order to form entanglement connections (or a logical Bell pair). In this paper, we focus on significantly reducing the overhead involved in logical CNOT operations, a fundamental primitive. We propose NOBOL, a novel approach that requires only one Bell pair to perform a logical CNOT operation on two distant qubits encoded in arbitrary CSS codes. More importantly, NOBOL only requires performing gate operations on the logical X or Z operator subsets of the logical qubits. For many CSS codes, such as the surface code, these subsets are significantly smaller than the size of the code itself. In this paper, we describe various circuit realizations of NOBOL, including a depth-optimal circuit with logarithmic depth in terms of the size of the logical operators. Finally, we propose effective methods to contain error propagation without incurring much additional overhead. Since NOBOL can be effectively applied to a wide range of quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes and, in addition, is agnostic to qubit modalities and effective for various architectures, including those based on either a monolithic QPU or distributed QPUs.

titles.title: Need One Bell-pair Only (NOBOL) for Low-Overhead Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing

abstracts.value: Precise calibration of LIGO's strain readout plays a vital role in our ability to extract information from gravitational-wave detections. We present a comparative analysis of two independent direct-force calibration methods: the Newtonian Calibrator (NCal) and Photon Calibrator (PCal) systems. Currently, LIGO relies solely on the PCal system as its absolute calibration reference. To facilitate comparison, a series of direct-force injections were performed using the NCal and PCal systems at the LIGO Hanford observatory just after the completion of the third observing run. We compute the ratio of the measured to expected strain amplitudes for every injection. For each injection frequency across a 30 Hz band, the ratios of NCal and PCal differ by $\sim$1%, demonstrating a small systematic discrepancy between the two systems. This difference highlights the importance of maintaining multiple independent calibration references to validate LIGO's calibration.

titles.title: A Tale of Two Calibrators: Comparing Newtonian and Photon Calibration in Advanced LIGO after the Third Observing Run

abstracts.value: Quantum walks spread ballistically but become diffusive with classical admixture. We compare two hybrid walks using identical quantum and classical steps at the same classical-step rate but ordered differently in time. Any nonzero admixture yields diffusion. Near the quantum limit, both diffusion coefficients have first-order poles, but their amplitudes differ by about a factor of two. The coherence timescale sets the pole order, while temporal organization sets the amplitude. We expect our analytical framework to apply broadly to quantum--classical hybrid systems.

titles.title: Universal scaling and protocol-dependent amplitude in hybrid quantum walks

abstracts.value: Today's quantum devices are noisy, so reducing circuit size is critical for reliable execution. Existing rule-based optimizers often rely on large rule sets that are difficult to manage and still miss long-distance transformations. We present QSymb, a framework for synthesizing compact and expressive quantum-circuit rewrite rules with formal guarantees. We formalize symbolic rewrite rules in which a symbolic gate represents infinitely many subcircuits. We then define canonical symbolic rules of the form $L;S = S;R$ and prove that they constitute a compact generative core from which general symbolic rules can be derived. On top of this formal foundation, given a gate set, QSymb synthesizes (1) a small, non-derivable concrete rule set that is complete up to chosen size and qubit bounds, and (2) a small but expressive canonical symbolic rule set that captures transformations beyond finite or monomial-only patterns. We further present rule anchoring to derive optimization-effective rules from canonical symbolic rules. Together, these results provide both expressiveness and guarantees: soundness of synthesized rules via validation, non-derivability, and bounded completeness. On the IBM-Eagle gate set, QSymb strictly outperforms state-of-the-art rewrite-based optimizers (Qiskit, Guoq, Quartz, TKET, and Queso) in two-qubit-gate reduction on 90%, 67%, 82%, 85%, and 83% of standard quantum algorithm benchmarks, respectively; on Nam gate set, the corresponding rates are 88%, 74%, 81%, 86%, and 82.9%. It achieves final average two-qubit-gate reductions of 27.44% and 29.95%, respectively.

titles.title: Synthesis of Compact and Expressive Quantum-Circuit Optimizations

abstracts.value: Advancing quantum information technologies requires qubits whose coherence can be precisely engineered. Among the qubit platforms in development, molecular spin qubits (MSQs) stand out for their atomic scale tunability and chemical specificity, making them powerful candidates for sensing, simulation, and information processing. However, integrating MSQs into solid-state architectures without degrading their coherence remains a central challenge. Here, we introduce van der Waals (vdW) confinement within two-dimensional materials as a strategy for stabilizing quantum states in MSQs by engineering their local electronic, vibrational, and symmetry environments. Using cobaltocene as a model system, we show that confinement within vdW SnS2 and CdPS3 single crystals reorganizes the single-ion energy landscape and slows spin-lattice relaxation by over two orders of magnitude relative to unconfined cobaltocene. The confined MSQs adopt deterministic orientations and self-assemble into ordered, atomically precise superlattices, establishing vdW confinement as a pathway for integrating MSQs into functional quantum devices.

titles.title: Molecular spin qubits in a van der Waals bottle

abstracts.value: In large-scale disaster scenarios, rapid localization of missing persons is a critical challenge for search-and-rescue (SAR) operations. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) equipped with radio frequency (RF) receivers can support RF-based localization by collecting signals emitted from mobile devices at spatially distributed sensing locations. This paper addresses the resulting waypoint-selection problem: determining a minimum set of UAV waypoints that provides at least threefold coverage of every potential target location. We formulate this task as an extended k-coverage problem that independently defines the UAV-navigable and target regions, and derive an exact-penalty quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) formulation with a sufficient penalty condition that preserves feasibility and minimum waypoint cardinality. The QUBO is mapped to an Ising-form cost Hamiltonian and evaluated using the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) on both a noise-free simulator and IBM's 127-qubit Eagle processor. On the tested simulator instances, QAOA recovers the known minimum-cardinality solutions. Across the rectangular hardware test cases, the mean 3-coverage ratio exceeded 95%. In the campus-scale evaluation, ten hardware executions achieved 99.3% mean 3-coverage with a 90% feasible-run rate, while the shortest feasible flight path was up to 37.0% shorter than those of the deterministic grid-based baselines. Additional comparisons with classical optimization and learning-based baselines are provided, together with computational and quantum-resource analyses for larger generated instances. These results establish an exact QUBO representation for RF-based SAR waypoint selection and characterize its implementation on current gate-based quantum hardware.

titles.title: Quantum-Based k-Coverage Optimization for UAV-Aided Search and Rescue Missions

abstracts.value: The halo nucleon-core system is, by definition, a shallow state nucleus. The nucleon, in most cases a neutron, is loosely bound to the other nucleons forming the core. Accordingly, the system is located inside the universal window; the halo nucleon most likely resides far from the rest of the nucleons, showing a remarkable insensitivity to details of the interaction with the core. The system can be described using a simple nucleon-core interaction, and this description can be extended to the nucleon-nucleon-core system. Specifically, treating the neutron-core and the neutron-neutron-core systems with a Gaussian interaction as a reference, we show trajectories inside the universal window governed by interaction parameters determined from low-energy observables, such as the neutron-core binding energy, scattering length, and effective range. In this way, we can relate properties of different halo nuclei that might seem uncorrelated. In particular, we determine the three-body parameter, the binding momentum at the unitary limit, and show that the two-neutron halo nuclei emerge from that limit following a linear trajectory depending on the neutron-core range.

titles.title: Gaussian characterization of two-neutron halo nuclei

abstracts.value: In the pulsed-power accelerators that drive Z-pinch implosions, multi-MA currents rapidly heat the electrodes above the threshold for plasma formation. When these surface plasmas are transported into the transmission line gap, they shunt some portion of the driver current away from the load, referred to as “current loss.” In highly magnetized systems, current loss is well approximated by a Hall current proportional to the minimum plasma density in the gap and the electric field [N. Bennett, D. R. Welch, G. Laity, D. V. Rose, and M. E. Cuneo, Magnetized particle transport in multi-MA accelerators, Phys. Rev. Accel. Beams , 060401 (2021)]. This paper explores the mechanism that drives the initial plasma transport into the gap, which is difficult to isolate in large-scale power-flow simulations but is instrumental in seeding the current-loss mechanism. The stability and dynamics of an electron sheath emitted from a resistive cathode plasma in the presence of large magnetic fields are investigated using semianalytic theory and simulation. A dispersion analysis determines that the instability growth rate scales inversely to ion mass and magnetic field strength. This scaling is confirmed in kinetic models of an electron sheath and resistive plasma using the relativistic electromagnetic particle-in-cell code CHICAGO<sup>®</sup>. The simulations are initiated with field magnitudes representative of the final feed of a Z-pinch driver and demonstrate that a resistive plasma instability grows on ns timescales, generating perturbed electric fields of sufficient strength to rapidly accelerate plasma ions into the gap. Although the resulting plasma density in the gap is 2 orders of magnitude below the surface density, it is sufficient to generate the published current losses.

titles.title: Electrode plasma transport into the gap of high-current Z-pinch accelerators

abstracts.value: In future storage rings, precise control of the electron-beam phase space will become increasingly important. A key challenge in these dynamics is maintaining the lattice’s isochronicity, which is crucial for applications such as optical stochastic cooling and steady-state microbunching. In particular, path-length deviations induced by intrabeam scattering (IBS) could limit the performance of steady-state microbunching light sources. In this paper, we present a more accurate formula for calculating the IBS-induced path-length deviation of an electron beam traversing the lattice, which can aid in lattice optimization. Additionally, we have developed a tool to simulate IBS-kick effects on beam dynamics. It can directly compute the IBS equilibrium emittance in storage rings and efficiently evaluate the associated path-length deviations for an electron beam traversing a lattice.

titles.title: Accurate calculation of path-length variation due to intrabeam scattering for an electron beam traversing a lattice

abstracts.value: The realization of stable, scalable room-temperature quantum computing is severely bottlenecked by the slow pace of materials discovery, which conventionally relies on classical Density Functional Theory (DFT) and trial-and-error synthesis. In this work, we introduce a Generative Quantum Machine Learning (GQML) framework to invert this paradigm, utilizing a 64-qubit parameterized quantum circuit to autonomously generate candidate material structures optimized for high-temperature quantum coherence. By mapping target properties directly into a quantum latent space, our model evaluated <math altimg="si190.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1144"><mrow><mn>1.5</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> structural permutations in just 45 QPU-hours—a 99.8% reduction in screening time compared to the estimated 120,000 CPU-hours required by traditional classical methods. The GQML pipeline identified 42 highly promising solid-state spin defect candidates with predicted operational viability above 250 K. Experimental synthesis of the top-ranked candidate — a novel carbon-boron-nitride hybrid lattice — demonstrated stable qubit coherence (<math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1162"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>∗</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">=</mo><mn>3.2</mn></mrow></math> ms) at 298 K (room temperature). Furthermore, the model predicted thermodynamic stability and topological invariants with an accuracy of 94.3%. This approach establishes a scalable, data-driven pathway for the rapid discovery and manufacturing of next-generation quantum hardware. •GQML framework rapidly identifies stable room-temperature qubit materials.•Evaluated 15 million candidate structures in 45 QPU-hours via 64-qubit PQC.•Quantum generative screening reduces computational time by 99.8% versus DFT.•Pipeline identified 42 highly viable solid-state defect candidates above 250 K.•Synthesized C-BN hybrid lattice demonstrates <math altimg="si107.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1212"><msubsup><mrow><mi>T</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>∗</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> = 3.2 ms coherence at 298 K.

abstracts.value: The Probe for LUminosity MEasurement (PLUME) detector is a dedicated luminosity monitor at the LHCb interaction point. It is a hodoscope comprising 48 Hamamatsu R760 photomultiplier tubes that detect Cherenkov light produced by particles travelling in the direction opposite to the LHCb spectrometer acceptance. PLUME provides real-time, bunch-by-bunch luminosity measurements during LHCb data taking and serves as the primary detector for controlling the luminosity levelling process at LHCb. In addition, its data are used offline, together with other dedicated counters from LHCb sub-systems, to determine the integrated luminosity delivered to the experiment. This paper reports on the detector's operational performance during the 2024-2026 data-taking period of Run 3. The integrated luminosity recorded by the LHCb experiment in pp  collisions at √(s) = 13.6 TeV during this period, as measured by the PLUME online luminosity counters for detector performance monitoring, amounts to  ℒ = (26.71 ±  1.07) fb$^{-1}$. The luminosity values used in physics analyses are determined separately through dedicated offline calibrations based on van der Meer scans and Beam Gas Imaging techniques, and will be reported in a dedicated publication, as they are beyond the scope of this paper.

titles.title: Operation and performance of the Probe for Luminosity Measurement at LHCb

abstracts.value: The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) is a next-generation long-baseline neutrino oscillation experiment. A critical component of the DUNE Near Detector (ND) is a Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LArTPC) called ND-LAr. ND-LAr employs a novel pixelated charge readout based on the LArPix ASIC, enabling native 3D reconstruction through self-triggering pixels. Unlike traditional wire-based readouts, the pixelated anode consists of a single collection plane without induction layers in front. As a result, the pixels can register induction signals from drifting ionization electrons well before they reach the anode surface, leading to pretriggering. To mitigate this effect, we introduce a shielding plane placed above the LArPix anode to confine the signal-sensitive region near the collection electrodes. A 3D field response simulation was developed to optimize the shielding geometry and evaluate its impact on signal formation. We present the shielding plane design and demonstrate its performance using cosmic-ray data collected with a LArPix prototype. The results show improved signal localization and suppression of pretriggering while maintaining high electron transparency.

titles.title: Design of a shielding plane for LArPix

abstracts.value: Recently, quantum-state texture has attracted increasing attention as a quantum resource with potential applications in quantum information processing. We derive tight lower and upper bounds relating the geometric texture of a superposition of $n\ge 2$ mutually orthogonal pure states to the textures of its constituent states and characterize the corresponding equality conditions. As an application, we determine the temperature-dependent attainable texture range of phase-generalized coherent Gibbs states in arbitrary dimensions. The coherent Gibbs state attains the lower bound at every positive temperature, whereas the upper bound is attained by appropriately choosing the relative phases of the energy-eigenbasis expansion coefficients of the phase-generalized coherent Gibbs state. For equally spaced energy levels, increasing the dimension lowers the scaled temperature at which the upper bound reaches unity, while the lower bound approaches its high-temperature limit of zero more slowly. These results provide a quantitative characterization of geometric texture under superposition and reveal how temperature, dimension and relative phases jointly determine the attainable texture range.

titles.title: Quantum-State Texture Estimation of Superposition States

abstracts.value: Recently, there has been considerable interest in studying quantum sensing near the critical points of a system evolving unitarily and undergoing a phase transition. However, there are many quantum systems in which dissipation is very important. The quantum phase transition in such systems results as a result of competition between nonlinearity, drive, and dissipation. These quantum phase transitions belong to the class of nonequilibrium phase transitions. In this work, we present a detailed study of quantum sensing of the system parameters near the critical points of a dissipative phase transition. We illustrate the key results by considering a coherently driven nonlinear Kerr medium interacting with environment. The first-order quantum phase transition is characterized by the closing of the gap in eigenvalues of the underlying Liouvillian. The steady-state sensing away from the critical point has standard quantum limit scaling with respect to the effective system size, whereas Heisenberg scaling is found at the critical point. The latter is subject to a critical slowing down. We have also examined sensing of system parameters using the metastable states and find better sensing performance at intermediate timescales, i.e., when the system has not yet settled in steady state. Detailed results on the scaling behavior in different time domains are given.

titles.title: Quantum sensing in the vicinity of dissipative phase transition

abstracts.value: We study the multifractal criticality in a generalized Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. The results show that the system supports not only critical phases but also reentrance multifractalization (REM). By mapping the hopping term to an effective potential, we analytically prove that although the model has no explicit unbounded potential, a hidden unbounded potential is actually present—this is the key mechanism driving the emergence of multifractal critical phases. Moreover, one can get a condition where the competition between the explicit and hidden unbounded potentials is exactly balanced. Under this condition, the multifractal critical phase vanishes, and the system returns to the extended phase. Based on this mechanism, we achieve both demultifractalization and reentrant multifractalization. Finally, we double-check the theoretical predictions through wave packet dynamics, and the numerical results are consistent with our theoretical analysis. This work broadens our understanding of how unbounded potentials induce multifractal critical phases, providing a theoretical basis for designing new systems with multifractal critical phases.

titles.title: Hidden unbounded potential and reentrant multifractalization in a generalized Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model

abstracts.value: The quantum geometric tensor sets the local relation between variations of external parameters and distances between states in Hilbert space. Its real and imaginary parts are, respectively, the quantum Fisher information matrix, which determines the ultimate precision bound in parameter estimation, and the Berry curvature. We study the geometry of SU(1,1) Hamiltonian eigenstates and propose two dynamical methods for extracting the components of the SU(1,1) quantum geometric tensor. A time-separated quench method extracts both the real and imaginary parts of the quantum geometric tensor from transition probabilities following two sudden parameter changes separated by free evolution, while a weak resonant modulation method relates quasiparticle production to the same geometric tensor. These results provide an operational method for measuring the local geometry of single-mode squeezed states and, in particular, for extracting the quantum Fisher information matrix directly from experimental observables.

titles.title: Quantum geometric tensor for the group SU(1,1)

abstracts.value: Accurate reliability assessment of interconnected and interdependent systems requires explicit representation of interaction mechanisms arising from shared components, load redistribution, feedback coupling, and correlated degradation. Classical system reliability theory is formulated using real-valued probabilities and combinatorial aggregation and therefore lacks an intrinsic mathematical structure capable of encoding interaction strength, synchronization, and pathway competition. As a result, redundancy and vulnerability in highly coupled systems are often mischaracterized. This study introduces a quantum system reliability (QSR) framework that reformulates system reliability as a complex-valued field. In the proposed representation, the magnitude of each component amplitude corresponds to postevent functionality, while the phase encodes interaction induced by connectivity, redistribution, constraint release, and dependency. Because classical reliability contains no inherent phase information, this work rigorously defines reliability phase. It develops two independent extraction strategies: (1) a spectral-domain formulation based on discrete Fourier analysis of reliability fields, and (2) a quantum-field formulation derived from divergence, curl, and geometry-induced flux operators. Component reliabilities are encoded as complex amplitudes, and system reliability emerges through interference-aware aggregation rules that generalize classical series, parallel and inclusion-exclusion principles. The formulation preserves exact classical reliability under neutral-phase conditions while enabling constructive and destructive interference in the presence of dependencies. The framework is validated using benchmark networks, including cascading IEEE-118 data and interdependent graph models, demonstrating improved alignment with functional system behavior compared to classical connectivity-based metrics.

titles.title: Quantum system reliability: A phase-encoded interference framework for interdependent and interconnected systems

The Witten Index and N = (2, 2) Worldsheet Effective
Theory of Non-Abelian Vortices

Soumyadip Nandi ∗

August 2026

Abstract

The Witten Index for the worldsheet theory of BPS cosmic strings in N = 2
supersymmetry gauge theories have been investigated. Starting from N = 2
supersymmetry alegbra with central charges, BPS bounds and representation theory
of short multiplets has been reviewed. Cosmic strings of codimension 2 is used as
the foundation for constructing the moduli space of the vortex solutions for both
abelian and non-abelian U(N) gauge theories. Major focus has been devoted to
calculating the zero-modes of the vortex moduli. For the non-abelian case, the
vortex moduli space acquires an internal orientational structure described by the
compact CPN−1, arising from color-flavor locking. The low-energy dynamics of the
worldsheet is governed by an N = (2, 2) sigma model with the target space
Mvortex = C× CPN−1. Using supersymmetry localization, it is shown that the
Witten index of this worldsheet theory, receives the entire non-trivial contribution
from CPN−1. The fermionic/odd contributions of the ground state vanish by virtue
of the Betti Numbers. The main result demonstrates that the index is a topological
invariant, protected by the BPS condition. This provides a non-perturbative link
between the bulk topological defect and the worldsheet supersymmetric quantum
mechanics.

1 Introduction
The interplay between supersymmetry and topology has produced some of the most robust
results in Quantum Field theory. An important example is the Witten Index - the trace
Tr(−1)F e−βH over the Hilbert space of supersymmetric theory. The Witten index , [1] counts
the difference between fermionic and bosonic ground states. Because non-zero energy states,
E ≥ 0 cancel in bosonic-fermionic pairs, the Witten index is invariant under continuous
deformations of parameters. This feature, makes the Witten index a particularly powerful tool
for extracting non-perturbative information about strongly coupled systems.

For supersymmetric theories, with topological solitons (defects) , this invariance acquires a
geometric interpretation. The moduli space which can be described as the space for
degenerate minimum energy configurations, often carry non-trivial topology. The Witten
index of the effective worldsheet theory becomes a characteristic number (integer) of this
space. This connection is particularly essential for BPS objects , [2] , [3] where the central
charge bound [4], ensures that the tension / mass of the vortices is protected against
quantum corrections and the moduli geometry is exact.

Cosmic strings (codimension 2) that arises from spontaneously broken gauge symmetries
provide the foundation for this connection. In N = 2 supersymmetry theories in (3 + 1)
dimensions, BPS cosmic strings preserve half of the bulk symmetry (4 out of the 8
supercharges) leaving an N = (2, 2) supersymmetric effective theory on their (1 + 1) -
dimensional worldsheet. The bosonic zero-modes correspond to the collective co-ordinates on
the vortex moduli space. The translational modes parameterize the position in the transverse
plane and the internal modes are associated with the orientation of the vortex in color-flavor
space. For n non-Abelian vortices in U(N) gauge theories with Nf ≥ N flavors, the two
moduli are the position and orientation in the plane. One complex co-ordinate C encodes
position, the complex space CPN−1 – a compact Kähler manifold encodes orientation.

The goal of this paper is to compute the Witten index for the worldsheet sigma model, Rσ

with the topology of target Mvortex = C× CPN−1 . We achieve this in three stages. Firstly,
the N = 2 supersymmetry algebra is reviewed in four dimensions. The role of the central
charges ( Section 2 and Section 3) and BPS bounds is emphasized.

Second, the vortex solutions and their moduli spaces are constructed from the Abelian Higgs
model to U(N) non-abelian generalizations. Major focus has been devoted to the counting of
the zero-modes and the emergence of the CPN−1 factor from color-flavor locking. Third, the
Witten index is introduced and supersymmetric localization is applied to show that the
path-integral collapses over a fixed point locus of a scalar supercharge, yielding the Euler
characteristic of the target space. The central result of the paper is stated in Theorem 9.2

∆ws = X (CPN−1) = N (1)
This result embodies several notable features. The non-compact C factor, parameterizing the
center-of-mass of the vortex contributes trivially to the index. This reflects the fact that the
index is a non-compactly supported invariant. By Hodge theory, the harmonic forms of the
Witten index - the odd degrees are eliminated by the Betti Numbers. Hence, there are no
fermionic degrees of freedom. The entire non-trivial dependence on the rank N comes from
the orientation moduli space CPN−1 . Moreover, the β independence ensures that this is an

3



exact result, receiving no corrections from excited states or quantum fluctuations. In this
sense, the Witten index provides a "topological fingerprint" of the BPS cosmic string.
The paper is organized as follows:- Section 2 and 3 reviews the N = 2 algebra and BPS

2 The N = 2 Supersymmetry Algebra in (3 + 1)D
For N = 2 supersymmetry, the derivation of supercharges is naturally understood as an
extension of the Poincare algebra. The Poincare algebra SO(1, 3) is generated by translations
Pµ (µ = 0, 1, 2, 3) and the Lorentz generators Mµν = −Mνµ. We are basing our work in
four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with metric ηµν = diag(−1,+1,+1,+1) The N = 2
supersymmetry algebra extends the Poincaré algebra by fermionic generators—the
supercharges. These generators transform as Weyl spinors under the Lorentz group and carry
an additional index under the R-symmetry group, which rotates the two supersymmetries into
one another

The supercharge Q, rather than being introduced by hand, poses a much more fundamental
question- what is the largest possible continuous spacetime symmetry algebra that still
contains the Poincare algebra and is compatible with quantum mechanics? The answer is
given by the Haag–Lopuszanski–Sohnius theorem , [5] which extends the Coleman–Mandula
theorem by allowing fermionic generators. Consequently, beyond the bosonic Poincare
generators Pµ, Mµν , we introduce the fermionic generators QI

two independent supersymmetries (the SU(2)R index), while α, α̇ = 1, 2 are the Weyl spinor
indices. Since these generators carry spinor indices, they transform in the (12 , 0) and (0, 12)
representations of the Lorentz group rather than as scalars or vectors.

2.1 Commutation with Translations

The first step is to determine how these generators transform under the translations of
spacetime. Since translations commute among themselves, [Pµ, Pν ] = 0, and since

3.1 Representation Theory: Long and Short Multiplets

The representation theory of this algebra depends crucially on whether m > |Z| or m = |Z|.

Long multiplets. If m > |Z|, both a†α and b†β act as creation operators. The result is a
multiplet comprising 16 states. This is known as a long multiplet. More generally, for N
supersymmetries, long multiplets contain 22N states.

7



Short multiplets. What is more interesting is what happens when m = |Z|. In this case,
half of the creation operators do not create anything. For example, when m = Z, the bα
operators must vanish on all states in the multiplet. Only a†α act as creation operators. The
result is a vector multiplet with 4 states, but now with mass m = Z. This is known as a short
multiplet.

For m > |Z|, all four fermionic oscillators aee non-null, and the multiplet is generated by four
independent fermionic creation operators. The resulting long-multiplet therefore consists of 16
states. At the BPS bound, m = |Z| , one eigenvalue of the supersymmetry operator vanishes,
rendering two of the four fermionic operators null. Only two independent creation operators
are left and the multiplet shortens to 22 = 4 states. Thus , the 1/2 BPS shortening reduces
the 16 - state long multiplet to 4 state short multiplet..

Therefore, BPS states can be defined as the states that saturate a lower bound on their energy
derived from the supersymmetry algebra and, as a consequence, they belong to shortened
(smaller) multiplets that are protected against quantum corrections.

3.2 Classification of BPS States

As mentioned above, a state |Ψ⟩ is called a BPS state if it saturates the BPS bound M = |Z|.
Such a BPS state must satisfy Q |BPS⟩ = 0 for the choice of auxiliary vectors that optimize
the inequality. This means that a subset of the supercharges annihilate the BPS state. The
number of annihilated supercharges depends on the type of bound saturated, leading to the

• 1

extended supersymmetry (N ≥ 4) or for special configurations where multiple central

4 Topological Defects
Definition 4.1. A topological defect in a field theory with vacuum manifold V is a field
configuration φ(x) that is topologically non-trivial i.e, it cannot be continuously deformed to
the vacuum configuration φ = φ0. This defect is classified by an element of a homotopy group
π(d)(V), where d is related to the codimension of the defect.

The codimension of the defect determines it’s dimensionality. A defect of co-dimension d in a
D-dimensional spacetime has a worldvolume of dimension D − d . The classification proceeds
via the homotopy of a vacuum manifold: point defects (monopoles, codimension 3), are
classified by π(2)(V), line defects (cosmic strings , codimension 2) by π(1)(V), domain walls
(codimension 1) by π(0)(V), and textures (codimension 0) by π(3)(V)

Remark 4.2. The topological definition guarantees the stability of the defect against
continuous deformations. No local perturbation can unwind a topological defect ; it can only
be destroyed by a phase transition in which the vacuum manifold V itself changes topology.
This stability is the deep reason why topological defects carry protected information that
survives quantization - a property which is going to be essential when we compute the Witten
index of the defect sector.

4.1 Why Cosmic Strings ?

Cosmic strings are the natural test case for our Witten index analysis for several reasons.
First, they are well-understood BPS objects with a rich but tractable moduli space (Section
3). Second, their worldsheet inherits supersymmetry from the bulk (Section 8), providing a
natural setting for the Witten index computation. Third, they are codimension-2 defects,
which means the worldsheet is (1+1)-dimensional and the Witten index machinery of

9



supersymmetric quantum mechanics and sigma models applies directly. Finally, the
non-Abelian generalization produces a worldsheet theory with a non-trivial target space
topology, yielding a non-zero Witten index.

b). The action can be written as S = {Q,V }, For some V which is Q-closed.

The main focus of the paper here is the standard result where the topological invariant of the

abstracts.value: The Witten Index for the worldsheet theory of BPS cosmic strings in $\mathcal{N} =2$ supersymmetry gauge theories have been investigated. Starting from $\mathcal{N} = 2$ supersymmetry alegbra with central charges, BPS bounds and representation theory of short multiplets has been reviewed. Cosmic strings of codimension $2$ is used as the foundation for constructing the moduli space of the vortex solutions for both abelian and non-abelian $U(N)$ gauge theories. Major focus has been devoted to calculating the zero-modes of the vortex moduli. For the non-abelian case, the vortex moduli space acquires an internal orientational structure described by the compact $ \mathbb{C} P^{N-1}$, arising from color-flavor locking. The low-energy dynamics of the worldsheet is governed by an $\mathcal{N} =(2,2)$ sigma model with the target space $\mathcal{M}_{vortex} = \mathbb{C} \times \mathbb{C} P^{N-1}$. Using supersymmetry localization, it is shown that the Witten index of this worldsheet theory, receives the entire non-trivial contribution from $\mathbb{C} P^{N-1}$. The fermionic/odd contributions of the ground state vanish by virtue of the Betti Numbers. The main result demonstrates that the index is a topological invariant, protected by the BPS condition. This provides a non-perturbative link between the bulk topological defect and the worldsheet supersymmetric quantum mechanics.

occupy exactly one slot forces the internal index to rank four, since a massive quark par-
ticipates in four interactions at once; the object is a rank-six tensor with 35 internal slots,
three of which vanish identically by gauge invariance. Gravity is deliberately absent from
the internal index: it sits on the left of the field equation, and including it on the right would
double count. We verify that the assignment is a genuine partition by checking that the
summed degrees of freedom reproduce g∗ = 106.75 — a check that caught a three-degree-
of-freedom double count between the Higgs doublet and the longitudinal W/Z modes. In
this language the Higgs mechanism is an exact transfer of three degrees of freedom between
slots, and metric contraction yields 32 equations of state separating the 9% of proton mass
sourced through the Yukawa channel from the 23% generated by the QCD trace anomaly.

Because a single G multiplies the whole sum, the contracted Bianchi identity forces
channel-dependent gravitational couplings to vanish identically, so the equivalence principle
becomes a prediction protected by geometry rather than an input.

A minimum length is implemented by smearing the source, leaving the metric propagator
of the effective description unmodified at 1/k2. We show this placement is forced rather than
chosen: chaining the theorems of Schoenberg and Bernstein, a smearing giving a positive
energy density must be a superposition of Gaussians, and every such function grows expo-
nentially in the physical timelike channel. With the smearing on the source, gravitational
propagation stays local, no ghost arises, and tree-level unitarity holds to

s = 1.126MPl.

We do not claim ultraviolet completeness; the framework is an effective theory whose cutoff
exceeds every scale it predicts by at least three orders of magnitude.

Solving the field equation with a profile whose logarithmic slope saturates the dominant-
energy bound gives a black hole with two horizons, minimum mass M0 = 3.0496MPl verified
to 0.01%, a temperature peaking at 3.6MPl and falling to zero at M0, all four energy
conditions satisfied, and Schwarzschild recovered to 5 × 10−4 at 103MPl. Exact unification
follows from two vector-like SU(2) triplets and a colour octet; the same triplets mediate
the type-III seesaw, and a Boltzmann integration verified across nine solver settings gives
washout efficiency κ = 4.943×10−3, at which standard thermal leptogenesis succeeds without
resonance.

The framework has two free parameters, both bounded. Threshold ordering, proton
decay and the requirement that primordial black holes emit X bosons before becoming
relics confine z to 8.50 < z < 13.18, within which the high-scale leptogenesis CP invariant
is fixed (this is not the PMNS phase and is not directly measurable); and requiring the
grand-unified vacuum to survive to the Planck scale without becoming unstable or hitting

breaking scalar and the scalaron. We state each prediction with the assumption it rests on,
list the claims we tested and withdrew, and specify what a Page-curve mechanism would

1 Introduction

General relativity and quantum field theory are usually reconciled, or fail to be, at the level
of the metric. This paper asks a complementary question about the source: what should the
right-hand side of Einstein’s equation look like once one takes seriously that matter consists of
several distinct interactions rather than one fluid?

The total stress tensor computes geometry well and answers questions of provenance badly.
That distinction is not idle. About 91% of the mass of ordinary matter is carried by the strong
interaction and about 9% by the Yukawa coupling to the Higgs; the equivalence principle asserts
these gravitate identically, and MICROSCOPE tests the assertion to η = (−1.5 ± 2.7) × 10−15

[Touboul et al., 2022]. The total Tµν has nowhere to record the distinction being tested.
A note on method. This paper is the product of a long working session in which most of

the effort went into finding and correcting errors in earlier versions of the framework. Nine
claims were tested and withdrawn; two were caught by external problem sets. We report
the withdrawals in Section 15 because a list of surviving claims without the discarded ones
misrepresents how the work was done, and because the discarded ones mark where the natural
traps lie.

5.2 The forced resolution, and its price

The conflict arises only because analyticity ties the two regions together. A static source has

smearing is a property of matter states rather than a factor multiplying the propagator, no

We state plainly what this does and does not do to the geometry, since it is the point
most easily misread. The smearing is a property of matter states. The spacetime metric
remains a classical c-number throughout this paper: no quantum propagator is assigned to gµν ,
no wavefunction of the geometry is introduced, and no quantisation of spacetime is invoked
anywhere. Equation (8) is a semiclassical equation, a classical geometry sourced by a quantum
expectation value, and every result below inherits that status.

The consequences are favourable: the propagator is 1/k2, so gravitational propagation is
strictly local and the small-scale microcausality violation of non-local gravity is absent; there
are no higher derivatives, so no ghost; and tree unitarity is that of plain gravity, saturating at
1.126MPl, a margin 59% wider than the propagator-based scheme afforded.

The price is ultraviolet completeness. We should be precise: pure gravity is one-loop finite
on shell because the divergence is proportional to R and Rµν , which vanish by the vacuum field
equations; with matter those read Rµν = 8πG(Tµν − . . . ) and the divergence survives. The
framework is non-renormalizable at one loop, and Goroff–Sagnotti [Goroff & Sagnotti, 1986] is
not even the binding constraint. Matter cannot cancel it: the two-loop term is the Riemann-
cubed invariant from graviton self-interaction, while the one-loop coefficients are positive sums
over non-negative field counts, so only the empty theory gives zero.

7 Unification, neutrino mass and leptogenesis

7.1 Adjoints, and two triplets

Complete vector-like multiplets shift all bi equally and change nothing; fundamental-representation
additions leave a 15% residual spread that two-loop corrections of 1–3% cannot close. Adjoints
shift bi four to six times more. This is the real reason the MSSM unifies; supersymmetry is
sufficient, not necessary.

The use of adjoint vector-like fermions for exact unification is not new. It was established
by Ibe and collaborators and developed by Aizawa et al. [2014], who add a single SU(2) triplet
and a colour octet, both Majorana, and use the triplet at the TeV scale as a non-thermal dark
matter candidate, obtaining MGUT ≃ 1015 GeV and a proton lifetime short enough that Hyper-
Kamiokande can explore most of their parameter space. Our field content differs in one respect
with large consequences: two near-degenerate triplets rather than one. That doubles ∆b2 from
2.667 to 5.333 and displaces the triplet mass by eight orders of magnitude, from the TeV scale to
∼ 1012 GeV. The displacement is what makes standard thermal leptogenesis viable here, and it
simultaneously removes the triplet as a dark-matter candidate, that role being taken instead by
the Planck relic. The two scenarios therefore share a technique and little else: different triplet
number, mass scales differing by 108, different unification scale, different dark matter, different
proton-decay reach, and no gravitational sector in theirs.

12 A negative survey of flavour mechanisms

The framework does not predict fermion masses, and neither does anything else. We surveyed
the field quantitatively; Yukawas span 3.4×105 for the charged fermions. Froggatt–Nielsen with
ϵ = sin θC reproduces all nine to a mean factor 1.4 using integer exponents, but nine chosen
integers replace nine chosen reals. Warped extra dimensions compress the six-order hierarchy
into bulk masses spanning 0.173, all O(1), at the cost of a fifth dimension. Radiative generation
would need 2.51 loops for the electron. Discrete A4 predicted θ13 = 0 and was falsified at 31σ
by Daya Bay.

We tested the minimal modular A4 model explicitly, with everything depending on one
complex modulus and no free coefficients. Scanning the fundamental domain over all mass
orderings, the best fit is τ = −0.420 + 1.195i with χ2 = 269: sin2 θ12 = 0.194 against 0.303
(9.1σ), sin2 θ23 = 0.248 against 0.451 (13.6σ), sin2 θ13 = 0.0232 against 0.0223 (1.5σ). The
predictive version is excluded.

13 The vacuum energy, and why no new symmetry can help

The cosmological constant sits with the geometry and needs no slot. What remains is the
vacuum energy of the matter fields. The partition permits a question a single number cannot:
the leading quartic divergence cancels iff StrM0 = 0. For the Standard Model this is −60; our
fermionic content worsens it to −88. Replacing the fermionic octet with four complex scalar
octets and keeping one fermionic triplet gives −2, and including the graviton’s two polarizations
gives exactly zero. We do not claim this as a symmetry: requiring two triplets, which unification
and leptogenesis both demand, breaks it again; StrM2 remains far from zero, leaving 10106

21



rather than 10120; and the scalar-heavy content pushes the asymptotic-safety indicator to g∗ =
9.4.

More fundamentally, no new symmetry can do the job. Cancelling StrM2 and StrM4

requires pairing bosons and fermions of equal mass. Coleman–Mandula forbids any S-matrix
symmetry relating different spins beyond Poincaré × internal, and Haag– Lopuszański–Sohnius
shows the unique extension permitting such generators is supersymmetry. The known loopholes
— no mass gap, no S-matrix, higher-spin, discrete — are all closed for a framework with a mass
gap, an S-matrix, spins 0–2 and continuous sum rules to enforce. We therefore treat Λ as a free
parameter, as all of physics currently does.

16 Conclusions

Writing the source of Einstein’s equation as a channel-resolved tensor is a change of bookkeeping
with concrete consequences. Requiring one slot per particle forces rank four and four channels
— the three gauge interactions of the matter Lagrangian plus the Higgs sector — and the
partition can be checked against g∗ — a check that caught a real error. The Higgs mechanism
becomes an exact transfer between slots; the trace equation separates the two routes by which
the proton acquires mass; and the single G turns the equivalence principle from an assumption
into a Bianchi-protected prediction.

A theorem of Schoenberg and Bernstein shows the minimum-length smearing must act on
the source, which keeps propagation local, avoids ghosts, and widens the unitarity margin, at
the price of ultraviolet completeness — paid explicitly, with every prediction three orders of
magnitude below the cutoff.

Most of the work went into finding and fixing our own errors, and the framework is sharper
for it. Four free parameters have become two, both bounded: z to a factor 65 in MGUT, and
the adjoint quartic to a factor of two around a value that αGUT itself selects. Four experiments
in the coming decade can each falsify it. Where we could not derive a mechanism we specified
one instead, which we regard as the honest form of an unsolved problem.

abstracts.value:
We write the source of the Einstein equation as a two-point, channel-resolved tensor whose internal indices label the four interactions appearing in the matter Lagrangian: electromagnetic, strong, weak and Yukawa. Requiring that every Standard Model particle occupy exactly one slot forces the internal index to rank four, since a massive quark participates in four interactions at once; the object is a rank-six tensor with 35 internal slots, three of which vanish identically by gauge invariance. Gravity is deliberately absent from the internal index: it sits on the left of the field equation, and including it on the right would double count. We verify that the assignment is a genuine partition by checking that the summed degrees of freedom reproduce g* = 106.75, a check that caught a three-degree-of-freedom double count between the Higgs doublet and the longitudinal W/Z modes. In this language the Higgs mechanism is an exact transfer of three degrees of freedom between slots, and metric contraction yields 32 equations of state separating the 9% of proton mass sourced through the Yukawa channel from the 23% generated by the QCD trace anomaly.

Because a single Newton constant multiplies the whole sum, the contracted Bianchi identity forces channel-dependent gravitational couplings to vanish identically, so the equivalence principle becomes a prediction protected by geometry rather than an input.

A minimum length is implemented by smearing the source, leaving the metric propagator of the effective description unmodified at 1/k^2. We show this placement is forced rather than chosen: chaining the theorems of Schoenberg and Bernstein, a smearing giving a positive energy density must be a superposition of Gaussians, and every such function grows exponentially in the physical timelike channel. With the smearing on the source, gravitational propagation stays local, no ghost arises, and tree-level unitarity holds to sqrt(s) = 1.126 M_Pl. We do not claim ultraviolet completeness; the framework is an effective theory whose cutoff exceeds every scale it predicts by at least three orders of magnitude, and the spacetime metric remains a classical c-number throughout.

Solving the field equation with a profile whose logarithmic slope saturates the dominant-energy bound gives a black hole with two horizons, minimum mass M_0 = 3.0496 M_Pl verified to 0.01%, a temperature peaking at 3.6 M_Pl and falling to zero at M_0, all four energy conditions satisfied, and Schwarzschild recovered to 5e-4 at 1000 M_Pl. Exact gauge coupling unification follows from two vector-like SU(2) triplets and a colour octet; the same triplets mediate the type-III seesaw, and a Boltzmann integration verified across nine solver settings gives washout efficiency 4.943e-3, at which standard thermal leptogenesis succeeds without resonance.

The framework has two free parameters, both bounded. Threshold ordering, proton decay and the requirement that primordial black holes emit X bosons before becoming relics confine z to 8.50 < z < 13.18, within which the high-scale leptogenesis CP invariant is fixed (this is not the PMNS phase and is not directly measurable); and requiring the grand-unified vacuum to survive to the Planck scale without becoming unstable or hitting a Landau pole confines the adjoint quartic to 0.16 to 0.61, with a renormalization-group attractor in 0.18 to 0.53 set by the unified gauge coupling itself.

The sharpest experimental proposal is a channel-separated equivalence-principle test. Using deuterated polyethylene together with two conventional pairs, the three couplings separate with condition number 38.2, bounding the trace-anomaly coupling to 2.5e-11: whether mass generated by the QCD trace anomaly, a purely quantum effect, gravitates like mass of any other origin. No experiment has isolated that quantity.

We also report a negative result: six attempts to derive the tensor-to-scalar ratio from the framework's own content all fail, the nearest by a factor of four, so the inflaton must be a field separate from both the GUT-breaking scalar and the scalaron. We state each prediction with the assumption it rests on, list the claims we tested and withdrew, and specify what a Page-curve mechanism would have to supply, having shown that the conservation law permits but does not force it.

titles.title: Quantum Relativity: A Channel-Resolved Energy Tensor as the Source of Gravity: Structure, Minimum-Length Regularization, Exact Gauge Coupling Unification, and Falsifiable Predictions

abstracts.value: The goal of this paper is to combine algebraic quantum field theory with methods from modal logic and the causal set program. We introduce a factorially damped past-influence operator on causal sets, formulate locally covariant nets over Alexandrov intervals, and give discrete analogues of the Haag–Kastler axioms. We close by sketching a route toward dynamics via sequential growth and incidence-algebra localization.

Background: Recent studies of the β decay of fission fragments by total absorption spectroscopy have found less decay energy attributed to leptons than previously believed, with studies of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> being particularly impactful for reactor decay heat. These results are also crucial for interpreting measurements of reactor antineutrino energy spectra.
Purpose: To obtain complete <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay patterns of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>. Determine the impact on reactor decay heat for all four isotopes and the impact on <math><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ν</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>e</mi></msub></math> emission calculation for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.
Method: The complete <math><mi>β</mi></math>-decay intensities of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tc</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Ru</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Rh</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> were measured with the Modular Total Absorption Spectrometer (MTAS) at Argonne National Laboratory. A beam of radioactive isobars with mass number A = 105 was produced by the CARIBU source and delivered to MTAS. Specifically, for <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, a multireflection time-of-flight device was employed to isolate a pure beam of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Mo</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>105</mn></mmultiscripts></math> nuclides before delivery to MTAS. abstracts.value: The fission fragment mass and total kinetic energy (TKE) distributions of neutron deficient <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tl</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>193</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, populated in the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Si</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>28</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ho</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>165</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">S</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>34</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Tb</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>159</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> reactions, have been measured at overlapping excitation energies. By employing a two-dimensional unbinned maximum likelihood fitting procedure, a substantial asymmetric fission fraction was identified across all measured energies with fragment mass centroids pointing toward the influence of deformed shell gaps near <math><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>≈</mo><mn>36</mn></mrow></math>. The extracted TKE values consistently cluster into two distinct groups, where the higher TKE associated with the asymmetric mode indicates a more compact scission configuration. While both entrance channels yield compatible asymmetric fractions, the experimental mass widths exhibit a systematic increase below the Coulomb barrier. This enhancement is more pronounced in the <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Si</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>28</mn></mmultiscripts><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mo> </mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Ho</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>165</mn></mmultiscripts></math> system, potentially reflecting a “double-deformation” influence from the oblate projectile and highly prolate target. Comparisons with the general description of fission observables (GEF) model show a systematic underprediction of the asymmetric component in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Tl</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>193</mn></mmultiscripts></math>, highlighting the potential for continued development of model parameters within this transitional mass region. These results provide critical empirical constraints and demonstrate that while shell effects govern the modal structure, entrance-channel deformations significantly influence the sub-barrier fission dynamics.

abstracts.value: We develop an algorithm to automatically design photonic gates and circuits that is based on a combination of optimization and pruning methods. It starts with a general ansatz for optical circuits with tunable parameters that are then subjected to optimization. The algorithm simplifies the final circuit by pruning its unnecessary elements following predefined criteria. We demonstrate the algorithm by producing both approximate and numerically exact implementations of the cnot gate and Deutsch-Jozsa, Grover, and Fourier transform two-qubit quantum circuits. All implementations of the different gates and circuits can be integrated into larger quantum information protocols.

titles.title: Automated design of photonic two-qubit quantum gates and circuits via optimization and pruning

abstracts.value: Diffusion-based large language models have recently attracted significant interest as a promising class of nonautoregressive generative models. However, their applications to quantum many-body systems remain largely unexplored. We introduce M-Diffushadow, a multimodal diffusion language model for quantum many-body systems. In M-Diffushadow, we adopt a full attention mechanism alongside iterative decoding, which better aligns with the physical characteristics of quantum systems and thereby enables a more faithful modeling of such systems. As a multimodal approach, M-Diffushadow enables bidirectional cross-modal inference, reconstruction from partially observed multimodal records, and fully joint generation without prior measurement outcomes, aligning naturally with realistic experimental constraints where measurement access is limited or incomplete. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework on the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model (TFIM), where generated data accurately reproduce ground-state energies and correlation functions across different phases. We further provide an additional numerical example on the XXZ spin chain to support the applicability of M-Diffushadow beyond the original TFIM benchmark. M-Diffushadow shows the potential to capture and analyze the complex quantum phenomena in quantum many-body systems.

titles.title: Multimodal discrete diffusion for quantum measurement generation in the one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model

abstracts.value: The forthcoming Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) requires precise modeling of neutrino--nucleus interactions to achieve its neutrino-oscillation measurement goals. GENIE, the Monte Carlo event generator used by DUNE and other Fermilab-based experiments as a central value model for neutrino-nucleus cross sections, exhibits known discrepancies in comparison to MicroBooNE cross section data, especially when considering neutrino scattering events' transverse kinematic imbalance (TKI). For quasielastic-like measurements, the data show a larger transverse missing momentum tail while maintaining a peak similar to that predicted by the baseline GENIE model. Previous attempts at a solution include variations of final-state interaction (FSI) strengths, incorrectly decreasing both the peak and tail, thus leaving the discrepancy unresolved. This work investigates whether inconsistencies between local and global treatments of intranuclear physics contribute to the observed mismodeling. In this work, GENIE FSI routines have been modified to directly utilize intranuclear particle positions, thereby introducing a newly localized momentum treatment in correlation with the nominal density in both the hA and hN intranuclear cascade models for their 2018 and 2025 variants. Meson-exchange-current (MEC) localization was also tested for the hN 2018 model. Comparisons of the intranuclear nucleons' ("scattering center") momentum and its radial dependence validate the localization implementation. However, while such consistent localization produces modest changes in the proton momentum spectrum at low-to-medium momenta, only small changes are observed in the TKI distributions. These changes are insufficient to account for the discrepancy with MicroBooNE data. Although a localized treatment improves the internal consistency of the GENIE model, the origin of the TKI discrepancy remains unresolved by such a solution.

titles.title: Studies of Localization Effects on Transverse Kinematic Imbalance in the GENIE Generator

abstracts.value: Lightweight channel attention mechanisms are widely used in image classification, yet their effectiveness in fine-grained visual recognition (FGVR) remains limited. Most modules summarize each channel by global average pooling (GAP), which captures activation magnitude but ignores spatial concentration, so channels with different spatial distributions but identical means receive the same descriptor. We propose Concentration-Aware Channel Attention (ConCA), which pairs the mean with a shift-invariant negative-input entropy (NegEnt), computed via a softmax over the negated activations, forming a dual descriptor that jointly encodes magnitude and concentration. A depthwise 1-D convolutional multi-layer perceptron (MLP), whose parameter count is linear in the number of channels, maps the pair to a per-channel weight. On six fine-grained benchmarks, ConCA improves over attention-free, SE-Net, and ECA-Net baselines as well as four richer descriptor-based modules under a controlled from-scratch protocol, and it generalizes across eight backbones on iNat2021-mini. These results indicate that the channel descriptor, together with the per-channel gating that maps it to attention weights, is an important but underexplored aspect of lightweight channel attention in FGVR.

titles.title: ConCA: Concentration-Aware Channel Attention for Fine-Grained Visual Recognition

abstracts.value:
The query-optimal algorithm of [CGWZ26] for general time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation uses 
$$ q = O\left( αT + \frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{\log\left(e + \log(1/\varepsilon)/(αT) \right)} \right) $$
 queries to $\mathrm{HAM\mbox{-}T}$ within $\varepsilon$ error for a Lipschitz-continuous time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$ on $[0,T]$ satisfying $\left\lVert H(t)\right\rVert\leqα$. However, its direct circuit implementation incurs a substantially larger gate overhead. In this note, we give an implementation of the same algorithm that retains its optimal query complexity and uses 
$$ O\left[ q \left( a + \log\left(1 + \frac{T(α+ βT)}{\varepsilon} \right) \right) \right] $$
 one- and two-qubit gates, where $a$ is the number of block-encoding ancilla qubits and $β$ is the Lipschitz constant of $H$. The main ingredient is an exact dyadic factorization of the ordered update product in the underlying one-query transducer.

titles.title: Gate-Efficient Implementation of the Query-Optimal Time-Dependent Hamiltonian Simulation

abstracts.value: Berlekamp's algorithm factors a squarefree polynomial $f\in\mathbb{F}_q[x]$ by deterministic linear algebra, reducing the problem to splitting an explicit commutative algebra $B\cong\mathbb{F}_q^r$ into its $r$ simple factors. For large odd $q$, the standard efficient splitting step is randomized, while known derandomizations are conditional on the Extended Riemann Hypothesis. We give an unconditional exact quantum implementation in a circuit model permitting single-qubit rotations through efficiently computable angles. The construction uses an unconditional counting argument. For a block containing $s\ge2$ irreducible factors, a quadratic-character test in odd characteristic and an absolute-trace test in characteristic $2$ yield a nonconstant test element with probability $p_{q,s}\ge\tfrac12$, known exactly in advance and depending only on $q$ and $s$, not on the unknown factorization. Exact amplitude amplification therefore converts each randomized test into a procedure succeeding with certainty after one amplification iteration. The resulting algorithm uses exactly $r-1$ quantum splitting rounds and $O(n^3\log q)$ quantum $\mathbb{F}_q$-operations and $O(n^3)$ classical operations, requiring no primitive root, quadratic non-residue, or distinct-degree preprocessing. The method also splits arbitrary finite-dimensional separable commutative $\\mathbb{F}_q$-algebras given by structure constants. Combined with R'onyai's classical structure theory, which computes the radical deterministically and reduces the remaining tasks deterministically to polynomial factorization, it yields the radical and the Wedderburn decomposition of $A/\mathrm{Rad}(A)$ into minimal two-sided ideals, with certainty, for any $n$-dimensional associative $\mathbb{F}_q$-algebra given by structure constants, using $O(n^4\log q)$ quantum $\mathbb{F}_q$-operations.

titles.title: Exact quantum splitting and the structure of finite algebras

abstracts.value: Using window theory, Bodzenta--Donovan showed that the derived category of a root stack $\sqrt[n]{X/D}$ has a $2n$-periodic $2$-term semiorthogonal decomposition. We define a categorical generalization of the root stack construction and interpret this as a pullback on the B-side of the 3d mirror symmetry equivalence of Gammage--Hilburn--Mazel-Gee. We analyze this pullback using categorical representation theoretic results of Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler and Ben-Zvi--Nadler--Preygel applied to SODs. We also show that the pullback is equivalent to a pushforward of perverse schobers on the A-side, allowing us to deduce periodicity from a simple decomposition of an A-side Lagrangian skeleton. Additionally, we adapt the construction of Bodzenta--Donovan to a new GIT problem, which yields an embedding of Coh($\sqrt[m]{X/D}$) into Coh($\sqrt[n]{X/D}$) for $m<n$ coprime, and prove $2n$-periodicity of the resulting $2$-term SOD.

titles.title: GIT for root stacks and 3d mirror symmetry

abstracts.value: We study the stabilizability of a N -level quantum systems using an indirect control ar- chitecture mediated by a noisy ancilla. After outlining the general theoretical framework for arbitrary N , we focus on the two-level case (N = 2), for which we derive a complete set of necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability. Finally, we illustrate the analyti- cal results with a simple numerical example on a two-spin system, showing convergence to a Bell state for a set of random initial conditions.

titles.title: Indirect stabilization of N -level quantum systems

abstracts.value: Fix the spectrum of a bipartite density matrix and randomize its eigenbasis according to Haar measure. We study the probability distributions induced on the spectra of the two marginal states. For arbitrary subsystem dimensions $m$ and $n$, the joint characteristic function of the reduced density matrices is expressed as a Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber integral whose external eigenvalues are the pairwise sums $x_i + y_j$. Repeated external eigenvalues are handled by confluent determinant limits. In the two-qubit case, we derive an explicit alternating-spline formula for the joint density of the two marginal Bloch radii. Its support is the Bravyi-Klyachko compatibility region. We also obtain a compact truncated-power formula for the Bloch-radius density of either individual qubit marginal. In the qubit-qutrit case, we derive a truncated-power formula for the qubit Bloch-radius density and a bivariate spline formula for the joint density of the largest and smallest eigenvalues of the qutrit marginal. The latter two variables determine the full qutrit spectrum because the trace is fixed. The derivations combine confluent HCIZ integrals, distributional Fourier inversion, orbital measures, and the SU(2) and SU(3) derivative principles. The resulting densities are piece-wise polynomial on chambers determined by subset sums of the fixed global eigenvalues, in agreement with the Duistermaat-Heckman description of projected coadjoint-orbit measures.

titles.title: Marginal spectral distributions on regular bipartite unitary orbits

abstracts.value: Quantum non-local games with quantum inputs or outputs have been formulated in several different languages, including rank-one and quantum XOR games, support maps between projection lattices, probabilistic quantum hypergraphs, and Frobenius-algebraic rule operators on finite quantum sets. We give a unified operator-algebraic comparison of these models by assigning to each rule its winning transformation space: the operator space of transformations accepted with certainty. We introduce \(\mathcal R\)-projection-test quantum games with finite-dimensional input and output von Neumann algebras and an arbitrary, possibly infinite-dimensional, referee von Neumann algebra \(\mathcal R\). Their winning transformation spaces are precisely operator spaces with a natural bimodule structure, equivalently rectangular quantum relations. We compare this formalism with projection-lattice games, hypergraph quantum games, and the graphical rule-operator definition. Projection-lattice games capture exactly the reflexive winning bimodules. Hypergraph quantum games admit value-preserving projection-test realisations, and, after passing to perfect transformations, describe the same reflexive part as projection-lattice games. Using Daws' technique, we also translate rule operators to projections in tensor products of finite-dimensional von Neumann algebras. This identification places graphical rules in the same operator-bimodule framework and preserves both values and perfectness. Finally, we compare concurrency with the synchronicity conditions of Goldberg and of Bochniak--Kasprzak--Sołtan. The framework is illustrated by classical, rank-one, quantum XOR, colouring, and quantum graph homomorphism and isomorphism games.

titles.title: Quantum non-local games: Quantum relations, projection lattices and rule operators

abstracts.value: We study the algebraic and differential structure of the Riemann curvature tensor of the higher-dimensional Kerr-NUT-(A)dS spaces, motivated by the eventual goal of finding an IDEAL (Intrinsic, Deductive, Explicit and ALgorithmic) characterization of this family of metrics. The special geometry of these spaces is governed by the principal tensor $h_{ab}$, a non-degenerate closed conformal Killing-Yano $2$-form, whose existence singles out the Kerr-NUT-(A)dS family; we therefore focus on the algebraic relationship between the Riemann curvature $R_{abcd}$ and $h_{ab}$. In our investigations we encountered an obstruction, which results in a no-go theorem: no non-trivial $2$-form, including $h_{ab}$ itself, can be constructed covariantly from the undifferentiated Riemann tensor alone. Despite that, we do characterize the family of Riemann-symmetric tensors that could be the curvature of a Kerr-NUT-(A)dS metric by an algebraic and a differential condition, stemming from the integrability of the defining equation of $h_{ab}$ and the second Bianchi identity. Our calculations apply in all higher dimensions, which becomes feasible by a judicious application of representation theoretic techniques related to a semi-direct product group $U(1)^n\rtimes S_n$ that stabilizes $h_{ab}$.

titles.title: Structure of the Riemann tensor in higher-dimensional Kerr-NUT-(A)dS spaces

abstracts.value: We extend the functional determinant approach (FDA), previously restricted to static impurities, to the case of finite-mass impurities by using the mass-gap description of Fermi polarons [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 193401 (2025)]. The quadratic structure of the mass-gap model enables the exact evaluation of many-body spectra and Ramsey dynamics for mobile impurities. We show that this mass-gap FDA smoothly interpolates between the Fermi-edge singularity for infinitely heavy impurities and the emergence of quasiparticle weight for finite impurity mass. Our results demonstrate that the mass-gap FDA provides a transparent and computationally efficient framework to describe the quantum dynamics of mobile impurities.

titles.title: Mass-gap functional determinant approach for mobile Fermi polarons

abstracts.value: Hydrogen-rich superluminous supernovae without narrow emission lines (SLSNe-II) are rare transients whose powering mechanisms remain debated, particularly the role of circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction. We present photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2019cqc to investigate its power source and progenitor mass loss. We model the lightcurve using MOSFiT with the csm and csmni models to constrain the explosion and CSM parameters. SN 2019cqc peaked at M$_{g}$ = −20.21 ± 0.07 and emitted ∼1.7 × 10$^{50}$ erg of energy in the form of radiation. Photometric and spectroscopic modeling indicates that CSM interaction dominates in both scenarios, with best-fit CSM and ejecta masses of ∼4.5 M$_{⊙}$and ∼32 M$_{⊙}$, respectively. The inferred CSM properties imply an extreme eruptive mass loss at a rate of ∼0.2-0.3 M$_{⊙}$, yr$^{−1}$ in the years preceding the core collapse, consistent with a variable progenitor of luminous blue variable progenitor. We observe a persistent blueshifted asymmetry in the Hα emission line. At early times (≲+110 days), this is attributed to electron scattering with the bulk velocity of ejecta, while the profile at late epochs (≳ +402 days onward) suggests the subsequent formation of dust in the ejecta. Additionally, we identify a distinct, short-lived feature at ∼4600 Å, likely a blend of ionized C iii /N iii lines powered by the interaction of the SN-shock with the extended atmosphere.

Hydrogen-rich superluminous supernovae without narrow emission lines (SLSNe-II) are rare transients whose powering mechanisms remain debated, particularly the role of circumstellar medium (CSM) interaction. We present photometric and spectroscopic observations of SN 2019cqc to investigate its power source and progenitor mass loss. We model the lightcurve using MOSFiT with the csm and csmni models to constrain the explosion and CSM parameters. SN 2019cqc peaked at $M_g = -20.21 \pm 0.07$ and emitted $\sim 1.7 \times 10^{50}\,\mathrm{erg}$ of energy in the form of radiation. Photometric and spectroscopic modeling indicates that CSM interaction dominates in both scenarios, with best-fit CSM and ejecta masses of $\sim 4.5~ M_\odot$ and $\sim 32~ M_\odot$, respectively. The inferred CSM properties imply an extreme eruptive mass loss at a rate of $\sim 0.2--0.3 ~M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$ in the years preceding the core collapse, consistent with a variable progenitor of luminous blue variable progenitor. We observe a persistent blueshifted asymmetry in the H$α$ emission line. At early times ($\lesssim +110$~d), this is attributed to electron scattering with bulk Velocity of ejecta, while the profile at late epochs ($\gtrsim +402$~d onward) suggests the subsequent formation of dust in the ejecta. Additionally, we identify a distinct, short-lived feature at $\sim$ 4600 Å , likely a blend of ionized C III/N III lines powered by the interaction of the SN-shock with the extended atmosphere.
